steps.what: Establish the testing scope, operational constraints and required coverage
Review existing security test procedures and relevant technical references
Choose test coverage, safe sequencing and stopping conditions
Develop the written security penetration testing processes

loop.purpose: Compose a process document around the tester's coverage and safety decisions
loop.input: selected reference passages and process design decisions
loop.output: draft process with traceable coverage and stopping rules
loop.check: Tester checks technical meaning, coverage gaps, target boundaries, prerequisites and safe stopping conditions before finalising the procedure
loop.stop: One draft and one correction; unsupported technical steps are written manually
loop.why_not_simpler: A fixed template supplies sections but cannot explain the chosen procedure across different network environments

steps.what: Validate the procedure in the authorised isolated test environment
Write validation findings and correct the process document

tasks.design: Use native search and procedure templates in {DOCS}, then draft the explanatory sections around the tester's explicit design decisions. Validation remains an authorised human activity in the {OTHER} isolated security test lab, with its findings written separately.
tasks.previous_blocker: Procedure authors repeatedly reconstruct standard sections around environment-specific choices.
tasks.enabler_now: A bounded drafting tool can reuse approved passages while leaving test design and validation with the tester.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing representative coverage and recognising unsafe assumptions about an unfamiliar environment.
tasks.human_edge: Judging whether a technically plausible procedure is safe and useful for the actual testing mandate.
tasks.altitude: Less prose assembly, with unchanged test-design and validation responsibility.

reach.task: Review whether a test process covers a network boundary
reach.learn: Network architecture and operational failure modes

evidence.claim: GitHub Copilot offers coding and review assistance with oversight; this supports tooling availability, not proof of safe penetration-test process generation.
The procedure-drafting design and all task-time estimates are model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary covers process development and isolated validation, including the process document and real validation findings. It does not execute an operational engagement or save deployment time.

The mandate and system owner supply allowed environment, prohibited actions, time window and escalation contact; s1 counts clarification. The tester produces coverage, prerequisites and stopping rules in s3 and records them in s4. Missing scope means manual clarification before any validation, not a guessed permission.

The {OTHER} category is an isolated security test lab. Its authorised target identifiers and procedure version are confirmed during s5; the full validation and final findings-write time remain. Existing lab runtime earns no human saving.
Test native document search and templates first. Ordinary process-document saves have no approval gate or separate saving; a gate binds the actual lab action to its allowed environment.
unknowns: Isolation and representativeness of the validation lab
research_questions: Does drafted process prose reduce writing effort without adding untested assumptions or unsafe prerequisites?

already_counted.description: Review source material, correct drafted processes, validate and record findings

incremental.description: Maintain approved reference passages and sample procedure omissions

approvals.approved_version: Exact procedure version, isolated lab targets, allowed actions and validation window checked before execution in s5; any change requires renewed human checking

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1: B=100, R=85, gross=15, upkeep=2, net=13. Cautious case: a new telecommunications environment makes all 15 reference hours necessary and procedure writing retains 26 of 30 hours; other 55 hours remain, giving 4 gross minus 2 upkeep =2. High 8 retains extra environment-specific rewriting.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Gather the vulnerability assessments and establish their scope and provenance
Compare findings across assessments and locate supporting evidence
Evaluate vulnerability validity and assessment coverage for the local environment
Choose the material risks and required further investigation
Write the vulnerability assessment evaluation and its supporting rationale

loop.purpose: Express the tester's evaluation in an evidence-linked record
loop.input: risk decisions and identified assessment evidence
loop.check: Tester checks exposure, uncertainty, evidence attribution and whether recommendations follow from the actual findings
loop.stop: One draft and one correction; missing evidence or contradictory claims return to manual writing
loop.why_not_simpler: Variable assessment prose requires explanation beyond a fixed severity field

tasks.design: Configure native finding filters and evidence views in the {OTHER} vulnerability assessment platform. Keep validity and risk decisions with the tester, and draft only the resulting evaluation narrative in {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Assessment comparison and evidence navigation interrupt substantive evaluation.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing assessment filters can group candidate findings; a bounded draft can express the tester's completed reasoning.
tasks.still_hard: Different scan coverage, false positives and unknown network exposure make similar findings non-equivalent.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguishing a relevant weakness from a scanner claim lacking local significance.
tasks.altitude: More evaluation time and less finding navigation; risk decisions remain human.

reach.task: Clarify whether a reported finding crosses a real trust boundary
reach.learn: Asset ownership and local network exposure

evidence.claim: Aikido Security provides code, dependency and cloud scanning; this establishes assessment-tool capability, not automatic validity of individual findings.
Native evidence filtering, evaluation drafting and the time estimates are model knowledge designs.

assumptions: Boundary evaluates already produced assessments and writes the actual evaluation. New exploitation, remediation and fix-result reporting are separate work; no speculative scanner runtime is counted as saved labour.

The {OTHER} category is the vulnerability assessment platform. Existing assessment producers supply report ID, target identifier, timestamp, finding ID, tool version, tested boundary and evidence reference. s1 retains source and scope verification; missing identifiers or incomparable coverage require manual comparison, never automatic risk conclusions.

The tester confirms candidate relationships in s2 and produces validity, exposure rationale and follow-up decisions in s3-s4. Capturing those decisions and correcting prose are counted in s5's retained 9.75 hours. Native grouping is a navigation aid, not an assertion that findings are duplicates.
Test native finding filters before custom integration. The evaluation's ordinary author save has no approval stage or click-saving claim.
unknowns: Assessment export consistency and evidence-link coverage
Availability of current local architecture and asset ownership
research_questions: Do native grouped views reduce comparison time without hiding differences in test coverage?

already_counted.description: Verify source assessments, confirm evidence relationships and correct the evaluation narrative

incremental.description: Maintain finding-view configuration and sample incorrect evidence linkage

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1: B=100, R=85.75, gross=14.25, upkeep=1.5, net=12.75. Cautious case: incompatible reports retain all 20 collection hours and 19 of 20 comparison hours, while evaluation writing retains 13.5 of 15 hours; other 45 hours remain, giving 2.5 gross minus 1.5 upkeep =1. High 8 requires better evidence links while keeping extra narrative correction.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Collect fix records and the corresponding verification evidence
Determine what the verification evidence establishes about each security fix
Prepare reports describing the results of security fixes

loop.purpose: Draft a report from verified fix evidence and tester conclusions
loop.input: identified fix records, verification evidence and conclusions
loop.output: draft results report with evidence references
loop.check: Tester checks that resolved, unresolved and untested outcomes remain distinct and that every conclusion matches the tested version and evidence
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unsupported resolution claims are removed and written manually
loop.why_not_simpler: Evidence captions and limitations need prose tailored to each fix, beyond a status-table export

steps.what: Check the complete report and confirm its internal recipients
Submit the final fix-results report to the internal security owner

tasks.design: Use linked records in {HELPDESK} and the {OTHER} security verification platform to assemble the report's evidence set. Draft the narrative in {DOCS}, then keep final evidence checking and the separate internal report submission with the tester.
tasks.previous_blocker: Verified fix outcomes must be assembled into a readable report with correctly attributed evidence.
tasks.enabler_now: Native record links reduce navigation, and bounded drafting can turn explicit conclusions into report prose.
tasks.still_hard: A completed fix ticket does not prove that the relevant weakness has actually been resolved.
tasks.human_edge: Explaining the limits of the verification and resisting unsupported closure claims.
tasks.altitude: Less report composition while retaining responsibility for evidence and conclusions.

reach.task: Distinguish implementation completion from demonstrated security improvement

evidence.claim: Evidence-linked drafting of security-fix reports and native ticket links are model knowledge designs; no digest case measures this particular report workflow.

assumptions: Boundary is reporting already completed verification, including the report write and actual internal submission. Fix implementation and retesting are not removed or counted twice. If a report is instead sent outside the organisation, the recipient check and external-send authority must be changed before deployment.

Fix implementers and verification testers produce ticket ID, affected asset, fix version, verification time, tested version, observed result and evidence reference through their existing work. s1 counts collecting and checking those fields; missing version or evidence returns to manual clarification, never automatic closure.

The {OTHER} category is the security verification platform. The focal tester produces conclusions in s2, corrects the narrative in s3 and checks the final report, recipient addresses and attachment version in s4. All capture and checking effort is retained in those steps.
Test native ticket links and report templates first. The ordinary draft save has no approval stage or saving. The distinct internal send is fully retained; no automated send is implied.
unknowns: Quality of fix-version links and verification evidence
Actual internal or external recipient boundary
research_questions: Does draft correction preserve unresolved and untested findings while reducing total reporting time?

already_counted.description: Verify the fix evidence and correct and check the final report

incremental.description: Maintain report mappings and audit unsupported resolution language

approvals.approved_version: Exact final report version, evidence attachments and internal recipient list checked in s4; any edit invalidates this send approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1: B=100, R=77.5, gross=22.5, upkeep=2, net=20.5. Cautious case: fragmented retest records retain all 25 collection hours and cautious outcome wording retains 30 of 35 drafting hours; all other 40 hours remain, giving 5 gross minus 2 upkeep =3. High 14 retains more evidence-caption correction than central.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Confirm the authorised environment and engagement-specific testing constraints
Select the relevant threat-actor techniques and safe test objectives
Develop the test scripts and engagement-specific test configuration

loop.purpose: Adapt existing test components to the tester's explicit design
loop.input: selected components, safe objectives and confirmed boundaries
loop.output: draft test package without execution authority
loop.check: Tester inspects target selection, side effects, cleanup, stop conditions and whether the code actually tests the intended technique
loop.stop: One draft and one correction; uncertain side effects or unsupported components return to manual development
loop.why_not_simpler: Engagement-specific script adaptation requires reading code and intent rather than filling identifiers alone

steps.what: Inspect the final package and verify its safe execution conditions
Execute the authorised tests and monitor their actual effects
Record the test evidence and explain deviations from expected behaviour

tasks.design: Use a bounded code draft inside the {OTHER} security testing workbench to adapt existing test components. The tester checks the final package and runs it within the actual authorisation; native run-linked evidence fields reduce separate transcription after execution.
tasks.previous_blocker: Engagement-specific adaptation and manual copying of test identifiers add work around safe execution.
tasks.enabler_now: Code assistance can draft adaptations, and native test-run records can reuse actual run identifiers.
tasks.still_hard: Side effects, imperfect emulation and changing conditions require active expert control.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing when a test should stop and distinguishing a valid emulation result from a misleading artefact.
tasks.altitude: Some script and evidence-entry work decreases; operational test control stays with the tester.

reach.task: Interpret whether observed controls respond to the intended technique

evidence.claim: GitHub Copilot supplies coding and review assistance with expected oversight; this is not evidence that generated security tests are safe to execute.
Bounded adaptation, native run-linked evidence reuse and all savings estimates are model knowledge designs.

assumptions: Boundary covers engagement-specific test design, scripts, checking, authorised execution and its actual evidence record. General process development in task 21752 is an input, not duplicate labour. Broader reporting is separate; the real evidence write remains here.

The system owner produces the existing authorisation: allowed target IDs, permitted activity, exclusions, time window and stop contact. s1 counts the tester's verification and clarification; missing permission prevents execution. The tester records chosen objectives and constraints during s2-s3, with their capture retained.

The {OTHER} category is the security testing workbench. The actual run creates run ID, test package version, target, timestamps and output references during s5; existing runtime earns no saving. s6 retains 10.5 hours to verify those fields, explain results and enter missing details manually. No inferred success flag replaces observed evidence.

Test native component libraries and run-record templates first. The model has draft authority only and cannot execute, expand scope or send findings. Ordinary evidence saves have no separate gate or saving.
unknowns: Reusable component coverage and actual manual adaptation time
Native run-record support and evidence integrity
research_questions: Does assisted adaptation reduce total development and correction effort while preserving scope and safe stopping behaviour?

already_counted.description: Correct drafted tests, inspect safe execution conditions and verify evidence records

incremental.description: Maintain permitted test components and sample generated-code defects

approvals.approved_version: Exact checked package version, authorised targets, activity bounds, execution window and stop conditions from s4; any package or target change voids execution approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1: B=100, R=86.75, gross=13.25, upkeep=2, net=11.25. Cautious case: a novel technique retains 24 of 25 development hours and unsupported run metadata retain 14 of 15 evidence hours; other 60 hours stay, giving 2 gross minus 2 upkeep =0. High 7 assumes reusable components but more code correction than central.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The tester spends less effort assembling procedures, scripts and reports while retaining scope control, evidence interpretation and execution judgement.
reach: Work with security engineers to connect test evidence to actual local control behaviour
skills_to_grow: Inspecting generated code for scope and side effects
Checking evidence provenance and tested versions
Measuring correction effort alongside drafting time
role.ambitious_version: Clearer, more reproducible security evaluations with human control of every operational test.
